title: A refresh rotation in flight during a password change or deactivation leaves the rotated session alive (cookie and OAuth)
failure_scenario: A user's laptop is stolen, or a cookie leaks. The user signs in elsewhere and changes their password, the documented way to end every other session. The stolen session's client refreshes in a loop; /api/auth/refresh has no rate limit. If one rotation is in flight when the revoke runs, its successor survives, and the thief keeps a sliding 14-day refresh family with fresh, valid access tokens indefinitely. The same holds for a connector's OAuth grant (30-day sliding). With a deactivation, the leftover row is refused while the account is inactive (auth.ts:217, tokens.ts:200) but comes back if a manager later reactivates the account. That contradicts members.ts:220-221 ('tokens minted before the deactivation stay dead').
